text: You pull into a busy parking lot, eager to get where you're going. You just want a quick, easy spot.
But the rows stretch on, full. You circle, then circle again, a growing sense of frustration taking hold.
Is it just your luck? Does everyone else always get the good spots? You start to feel singled out by the universe.
Finally, a miracle! A single, perfect space opens up, seemingly just for you. You swoop in, victorious.
That feeling of winning the last spot? It's no accident. Parking lots are designed to operate near capacity.

This scarcity makes each available space feel incredibly valuable, even though many spots open and close constantly. Now you know it's not just luck, it's the system perfectly leveraging human psychology.
